In [[fluid dynamics]] the '''Milne-Thomson circle theorem''' or the '''circle theorem''' is a statement giving a new [[stream function]] for a fluid flow when a cylinder is placed into that flow.<ref>{{cite book|last=Batchelor|first=George Keith|authorlink=George Batchelor|title=An Introduction to Fluid Dynamics|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Rla7OihRvUgC&q=an+introduction+to+fluid+dynamics|year=1967|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|isbn=0-521-66396-2|page=422}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Raisinghania|first=M.D.|title=Fluid Dynamics|date=December 2003|publisher=S. Chand |isbn=9788121908696|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wq3TU5tArTkC&dq=milne+thomson+circle+theorem&pg=PA211}}</ref> It was named after the [[United Kingdom|English]] mathematician [[L. M. Milne-Thomson]].

Let <math>f(z)</math> be the [[Potential flow|complex potential]] for a fluid flow, where all [[Mathematical singularity|singularities]] of <math>f(z)</math> lie in <math>|z| > a</math>. If a circle <math>|z| = a</math> is placed into that flow, the complex potential for the new flow is given by<ref>{{cite thesis|last=Tulu|first=Serdar|title=Vortex dynamics in domains with boundaries|url=http://library.iyte.edu.tr/tezler/doktora/matematik/T000958.pdf|year=2011}}</ref>

: <math>w = f(z) + \overline{f\left( \frac{a^2}{\bar{z}} \right)} = f(z) + \overline f\left( \frac{a^2}{z} \right).</math>

with same singularities as <math>f(z)</math> in <math>|z| > a</math> and  <math>|z| = a</math> is a streamline. On the circle <math>|z| = a</math>, <math>z\bar z = a^2</math>, therefore

:<math>w = f(z) + \overline{f(z)}.</math>

==Example==
Consider a uniform irrotational flow <math>f(z) = Uz</math> with velocity <math>U</math> flowing in the positive <math>x</math> direction and place an infinitely long cylinder of radius <math>a</math> in the flow with the center of the cylinder at the origin. Then <math>f\left(\frac{a^2}{\bar z}\right) = \frac{Ua^2}{\bar z}, \ \Rightarrow \ \overline{f\left( \frac{a^2}{\bar{z}} \right)} = \frac{Ua^2}{ z}</math>, hence using circle theorem,

:<math>w(z) = U \left(z + \frac{a^2}{z}\right)</math>

represents the complex potential of uniform flow over a cylinder.
